intro: Lesson 46. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: وَٱلْعَٰدِيَٰتِ ضَبْحًۭا (١) فَٱلْمُورِيَٰتِ قَدْحًۭا (٢) فَٱلْمُغِيرَٰتِ صُبْحًۭا (٣) فَأَثَرْنَ بِهِۦ نَقْعًۭا (٤)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: And the producers of sparks [when] striking

keywords.def: the panting breath of a running horse

questions.q: Chunk and link Al-'Adiyat 100:1-4 with the teacher.
Listening turns: today's group says 100:1-4 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: say it softly 3 times looking, 3 times without.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: Tell a grown-up what the horses in Al-'Adiyat do.
questions.a: They run, pant, strike sparks and raise dust.
A) horses running fast. 100:1: 'By the racers, panting.'

questions.q: Think again: Have you ever seen a horse run very fast? What can you hear and see?
questions.a: Panting breath, hooves striking sparks, dust flying: Allah swears by these horses in Al-'Adiyat.
